successCriteria.description: src/modules/leave/leave.service.ts exports ILeaveService and LeaveService exposing create, submit, approve, and reject operations that orchestrate the DRAFT → SUBMITTED → APPROVED/REJECTED workflow.
create persists a LeaveRequest in DRAFT status with requestedDays derived from the shared requestedDays(startDate, endDate) helper (never re-derived locally).
submit transitions a DRAFT request to SUBMITTED and increments the employee's pendingDays for the matching balance; a non-DRAFT request is rejected with a typed error.

approve runs inside PgUnitOfWork.withTransaction and atomically performs: status → APPROVED (with approverId/decidedAt), pendingDays decrement + usedDays increment, an audit-log insert, and a synchronous notification insert.

reject runs inside PgUnitOfWork.withTransaction and atomically performs: status → REJECTED (with approverId/decidedAt), pendingDays decrement only, an audit-log insert, and a synchronous notification insert.
src/modules/leave/leave.routes.ts registers Fastify routes that call the LeaveService directly (matching src/modules/uptime/uptime.routes.ts), with no separate controller file.
src/modules/leave/index.ts re-exports the public surface (model, repository, service) so other modules import leave only through its entry point.

constraints: The approve/reject unit of work MUST run inside PgUnitOfWork.withTransaction (from src/shared/db/unit-of-work.ts); the service receives IUnitOfWork via constructor injection and never imports a pool, client, or module-level db helper.
requestedDays MUST be computed via the shared requestedDays helper (canonical source src/shared/types/index.ts) — never re-derived in the leave service.
Routes call the service DIRECTLY (matching src/modules/uptime/uptime.routes.ts); no separate controller file may be created.
All cross-module imports go through each module's public index.ts only (balance, audit, notification, validation, employee, shared types/errors/db) — never into module internals.
Participating repository/service methods take the transaction client as an optional LAST parameter and fall back to the shared pool when omitted; withTransaction is never placed on a repository.
Every state-changing operation (create, submit, approve, reject) writes an audit record (GP-002); notifications are synchronous direct inserts, no BullMQ.
No tests may be created in this sub-phase (unit/integration tests belong to Phase 6c).
outOfScope: src/modules/leave/leave.model.ts and src/modules/leave/leave.repository.ts (Phase 6a — already delivered by a sibling sub-phase).
Unit/integration tests for the leave service (tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.service.test.ts — Phase 6c).
Cancel operation and CANCELLED status handling (not in this sub-phase's create/submit/approve/reject scope).
RBAC middleware/guards and JWT auth wiring (enforced at route level per GP-005, but the guard implementation itself is not a deliverable of this sub-phase).

ambiguities.description: Whether the leave service should expose a list/query operation (findByQuery) in this sub-phase, given the repository already supports it but the intent only names create/submit/approve/reject.
options: Include a read-only list operation in ILeaveService
Omit list — repository query is consumed by a later phase

ambiguities.description: How the service resolves the employee's balance for the request's leave type/period (which balance row to mutate) — the balance module exposes findByKey/getBalance but no explicit "current open period" resolver.
options: Service locates the balance via IBalanceRepository.findByKey using the request's dates
Service uses IBalanceService.getBalance with a derived period
Defer balance-location to a later phase and mutate by explicit balance id

ambiguities.description: Whether approval authorization (manager-of-requester check, no self-approval) is enforced inside the service or left to route-level RBAC middleware.
options: Both: middleware for role, service for manager/self-approval

entityInvariants.invariant: Lifecycle is strictly DRAFT → SUBMITTED → APPROVED|REJECTED (CANCELLED out of scope here); a request may only be submitted from DRAFT, and only a SUBMITTED request may be approved or rejected.
requestedDays is always the canonical inclusive day count (endDate - startDate + 1) computed by the shared helper; the service never stores a locally-derived value.
Reservation lifecycle: submit increments pendingDays; approve decrements pendingDays and increments usedDays; reject decrements pendingDays only — counters must never go negative.
Every state-changing leave operation (create/submit/approve/reject) produces exactly one AuditLog row with the correct AuditAction (CREATE/UPDATE/APPROVE/REJECT) and the actor as actorId.
Approve/reject produces a synchronous Notification insert (status PENDING) inside the same transaction as the status change and balance update.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Requires an authenticated actor (EMPLOYEE or above); the created request's employeeId is the requester.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Invalid input → ValidationError (400); insufficient balance → ConflictError (409).

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Requires an authenticated actor; only the request's owner may submit.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Unknown request → NotFoundError (404); invalid state transition (not DRAFT) → ConflictError (409).

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Requires MANAGER or ADMIN; no self-approval; approver must be the requester's manager or an ADMIN.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Unknown request → NotFoundError (404); invalid state transition (not SUBMITTED) → ConflictError (409); unauthorized actor → ForbiddenError (403).

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Requires MANAGER or ADMIN; no self-rejection; approver must be the requester's manager or an ADMIN.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Unknown request → NotFoundError (404); invalid state transition (not SUBMITTED) → ConflictError (409); unauthorized actor → ForbiddenError (403).

consistencyRequirements.requirement: requestedDays must be computed by calling the canonical requestedDays(startDate, endDate) helper — the single source of truth is src/shared/types/index.ts (the validation module imports it from there rather than re-exporting it).
The approve/reject transaction must use IUnitOfWork.withTransaction exactly as defined (service owns the boundary, data-access opens it); match the signature and client-forwarding pattern.
Balance updates must go through IBalanceRepository.update with the same Partial<Omit<LeaveBalance,'id'>> changes shape and optional trailing PoolClient.
Audit inserts must use IAuditService.record(input, client?) with CreateAuditLogInput (actorId, action, entityType, entityId, beforeState, afterState) and forward the transaction client.
Notification inserts must use INotificationService.create(input, client?) with CreateNotificationInput and forward the transaction client (status defaults to PENDING).
Leave persistence must go through ILeaveRepository (create/findById/update) with the exact 12-field LeaveRequest shape and UpdateLeaveRequestDto changes.
Route handlers must follow the direct-service-call pattern (instantiate service, call it, map AppError to status codes) rather than a controller layer.

integrationPoints.why: LeaveService reads and mutates LeaveBalance (pendingDays/usedDays) during submit/approve/reject via IBalanceRepository/IBalanceService.
LeaveService writes an AuditLog for every state-changing operation (GP-002).
LeaveService inserts synchronous notifications on approve/reject within the transaction.
LeaveService delegates date-range and balance-sufficiency validation (and derives requestedDays via the shared helper).
LeaveService resolves the requester/approver (manager relationship, self-approval guard) via IEmployeeService.
LeaveService injects IUnitOfWork and runs approve/reject inside withTransaction.
